title: Cross-functional Field Guide for Rolling a New Model into Catalog
creator: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:
A compact, role-oriented field guide for shipping a new model into Redwood's catalog. This ticket coordinates cross-team acceptance criteria, release notes, benchmarks sign-off, docs and comms assets, and the staged rollout plan for the first wave of customers. The goal is to provide a repeatable checklist that reduces ambiguity and centralizes owners for each artifact.

Scope / What this covers:
- Catalog entry creation and metadata hygiene (model card, tags, compatible runtimes)
- Benchmarking run, regression checks, and quality gate decisions
- Developer docs, quickstarts, and SDK/endpoint examples
- Release notes authored and localized (EN + EU-FR draft)
- Internal enablement: support runbook, sales FAQ, pricing guidance
- Announcement copy for blog, docs changelog, and product updates
- Rollout plan: canary cohort, telemetry targets, and rollback criteria

Checklist (owners and acceptance criteria):
1) Catalog + Model Card (owner: Product)
   - Draft model card with architecture, dataset provenance, quantization profile, and expected token cost.
   - Add compatibility matrix: supported API primitives (chat/generate/embeddings), max context length, known failure modes.
   - Acceptance: model card reviewed by Applied ML + Legal; model metadata validated in catalog UI staging.

2) Benchmarks & Quality Gate (owner: Research/Applied ML)
   - Run latency, throughput, and quality benchmarks on hosted and dedicated variants. Include 99th-pct latency and median tokens/sec.
   - Evaluate model on 3 canonical Redwood prompt suites and the customer-facing benchmark set.
   - Acceptance: no regression >5% in quality metrics vs baseline; performance within target SLOs. Publish benchmark report (link in attachments).

3) Docs & Quickstarts (owner: Developer Docs)
   - Update API examples, SDK snippets (Python/TS), and migration notes if new behavior introduced.
   - Add a short Quickstart for the model that demonstrates streaming and function-calling where applicable.
   - Acceptance: Docs reviewed in staging by DX and Engineering; code samples run in CI.

4) Release Notes & Announcements (owner: Product Marketing)
   - Author release notes with technical callouts, typical latency/cost, and recommended use-cases. Prepare three variants: short banner, technical note, and customer-facing blog draft.
   - Localize critical strings for EU-FR and JP as optional follow-up.
   - Acceptance: Copy approved by Product and Comms; marketing channel owners sign off.

5) Observability & Rollout Gates (owner: SRE/Monitoring)
   - Add per-model dashboards: token cost, per-route latency, error budget burn, and quality regressions (synthetic prompts).
   - Define rollout canary: initial 3% traffic, 48-hour observation window, automated rollback if any of: error rate >1% above baseline, 99th-pct latency increase >20%, or quality regression detected.
   - Acceptance: Dashboards provisioned in staging; alert rules tested in alpha cluster.

6) Support & Sales Enablement (owner: Customer Ops / Sales Ops)
   - Produce one-pager with recommended pricing tiers, comparators, and troubleshooting steps.
   - Prepare a short training session (30 min) and record a session for internal knowledge base.
   - Acceptance: Enablement materials uploaded and session scheduled.

7) Legal & Compliance (owner: Security & Legal)
   - Confirm dataset disclosure language and export control considerations. Ensure KMS usage guidance is clear for private deployments.
   - Acceptance: Legal sign-off recorded in the ticket.

Rollout timeline (high-level):
- Week 1 (2026-03-10 to 2026-03-16): Benchmarks + model card draft + docs initial PRs
- Week 2 (2026-03-17 to 2026-03-23): Observability dashboards, release notes draft, internal enablement, legal sign-off
- Week 3 (2026-03-24 to 2026-03-30): Canary rollout + monitoring window, prepare blog and marketing assets for public announcement

Rollout metrics & success criteria:
- Telemetry: 99th-pct latency within target, error rate stable, token cost within projected bounds
- Quality: Benchmark pass rate >=95% on canonical prompts; no customer-facing regression reports in first 72 hours
- Adoption: 50 pilot users onboarded in wave 1 or equivalent API usage (tokens or requests)

Staging links & artifacts (add links to attachments):
- Draft model card: https://confluence.redwood.ai/model-cards/pm-21001
- Benchmark report (staging): https://drive.redwood.ai/benchmarks/pm-21001-benchmark.pdf
- Docs PR: https://github.com/redwood-inc/docs/pull/1287
- Release notes draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/RELEASE-NOTES-PM-21001

Open blockers / risks:
- Kernel optimization regression may increase latency on some dedicated configs (ENG-4298). Engineering already triaging but may delay canary.
- Localization capacity constrained for EU-FR; may ship EN first but note in communications.
- Security review required for dataset provenance statements; Legal ETA 2026-03-18.

Next actions (owners assigned):
- Applied ML: finalize benchmark artifact and upload to Drive (due 2026-03-12).
- Developer Docs: open PR for examples and run CI (due 2026-03-14).
- SRE: provision dashboards and test alert rules in staging (due 2026-03-16).
- Product Marketing: draft release notes and blog outline (due 2026-03-17).

Notes from recent reviews:
- 2026-03-11 (Design review by Lucia Gomez): "Ensure the catalog thumbnail and tag taxonomy align with the new tagging guidelines; DM with DES team for taxonomy updates."
- 2026-03-12 (Engineering comment by Priya Nair): "Benchmark shows 8% slower tail latency on older GPU types; recommend adding guidance to release notes about dedicated vs hosted expectations."
- 2026-03-13 (Legal sign-off pending comment by Jordan Weiss): "Need explicit dataset provenance blurb; suggest templated phrasing to accelerate sign-off."

Contact list (owners for quick reference):
- Product (owner): Aarav Patel <aarav@redwood.ai>
- Applied ML lead: Priya Nair <priya@redwood.ai>
- Developer Docs: Lucia Gomez <lucia@redwood.ai>
- SRE/Monitoring: Daniel Park <daniel@redwood.ai>
- Product Marketing: Simone Laurent <simone@redwood.ai>
- Legal/Security: Jordan Weiss <jordan@redwood.ai>

Acceptance & close criteria:
- All owners have marked tasks as Done and linked artifacts exist in attachments.
- Canary completes without hitting rollback conditions for 72 hours.
- Release notes and docs are published and indexed in the public docs site.

If anything blocks sign-off, escalate to the Model Catalog PM thread and schedule a 15-minute sync with all owners.
